hardware.engine: Godot 4.7 custom, same executable as stable 1.5.0

puddle_visual_review.comparison: Same map, site, light, camera and wetness as the rejected broad blue-patch candidate. Smaller isolated standing-water patches retain the underlying ground colour.

discarded_optimization.reason: The broader query change was withdrawn during regression testing; original plane selection is retained. A later diagnostic traced the intermittent camera test gap to camera changes in deferred post-draw callbacks after the reflection process. The final fixture moves at process start and verifies the first submitted frame, retaining its interpolation negative control.

method: The complete scene renders in a 3840x2160 SubViewport; normal rendering stays enabled and the blank root excludes large desktop presentation transfers. Cloud and water clocks and camera paths are deterministic. Readbacks occur outside the timed loop.

Mines: private quicksave, first-person and overhead cameras follow a 45-metre cosine sweep over eight simulated seconds; 960 timed frames per case, eight seconds settling, forty later GPU timestamp samples. Visual-effect streaming continues; AI, simulation and local host are stopped. This is a rendering camera sweep, not an end-to-end gameplay replay.

Shoreline: 240 frames per case after four seconds settling and forty later GPU timestamp samples. Baseline contains the full on/off matrix; final pack confirms both effects on at the same two camera poses.
render_cpu_ms is an individual renderer timing probe, not a median. GPU main-view timestamps exclude the separately reported shadow/reflection viewports.

Cloud reflection cache remains 256x144 at 4K and high-quality ray samples are unchanged. Its unused radiance cube is reduced to 32; the two final reflected-sky samples match the corresponding baseline images byte for byte.

Particle scheduling compares serial, full-pool and bounded-pool execution over identical seeded simulation and draw-buffer work. All final particle records, RNG states, draw bytes, bounds and lifetimes must match. Timing excludes 60 warm-up rounds and records 240 further rounds per case.

Puddle tests render exposed flat terrain from isometric and shallow angles with original detail and detailed HD terrain, wetness held after rain stops, gradual drying, dry ground, the option disabled and roof coverage. Full-wetness visible coverage is bounded to keep standing water sparse. The revised captures were visually inspected.

Retained cloud ownership, projection, reflection-contract and particle microbenchmark results precede the final puddle appearance change; the corresponding feature implementations are unchanged. Per-build source hashes distinguish those packs. Final camera regressions, puddle captures and performance sweeps use the shipping pack.

Forced-draw diagnostics with the rendering loop disabled are excluded, because pending resource updates can add an engine draw. Experimental live-simulation viewport fixtures with stale GPU timing are also excluded from performance claims.
limits: No Windows/D3D12 or RTX 4090 laptop measurement is available. Linux Vulkan results do not guarantee the same FPS gain on another driver or GPU.
The Mines endpoints have no visible reflective water. This sweep isolates shadow-related CPU overhead and traversal rendering; reflected-water cost is measured at the shoreline.
Rendering and particle scheduling improvements do not establish that every gameplay stutter has been eliminated. No complete end-to-end gameplay FPS claim is made.
Steep-angle reflections remain subtler than grazing-angle reflections. Puddles use the existing wet-surface shading, not a separate planar scenery mirror.
No original game content, private save or video is included in published artifacts.
